messages:
maya (support): Heads-up: CartoMart (dedicated pool carto-prod-us) reporting sustained 429s and high 95th pct latency after a marketing email blast ~09:12 UTC. They say tokens-per-second SLO was violated and their burst credits were drained immediately. I have request/response logs and a billing delta showing negative refills. Can oncall + infra triage?

jon (oncall): Ack. I'm looking at the admission controller logs now. Any repro steps from CartoMart or sample traffic shape?

maya (support): They repro'd by replaying the exact burst: 20k concurrent short chat completions over 3 min. Steps: post /v1/generate with prompt batch, client-side retries at 2s. They also used streaming responses "chat.stream" for a subset.

ana (sre): @maya can you paste the admission controller lines (masked) and the pool headroom metrics? Need to know if admission rejected or auth/billing prevented admission.

maya (support): Pasting sanitized logs:

```
[09:12:03] admission_controller: request_id=abc123 account=cartomart pool=carto-prod-us tokens=1200 status=admit
[09:12:04] admission_controller: request_id=abc124 account=cartomart pool=carto-prod-us tokens=1400 status=admit
[09:12:10] admission_controller: request_id=abc150 account=cartomart pool=carto-prod-us tokens=800 status=admit
[09:12:11] admission_controller: request_id=abc151 account=cartomart pool=carto-prod-us tokens=600 status=admit
[09:12:12] admission_controller: request_id=abc160 account=cartomart pool=carto-prod-us tokens=900 status=deny reason=burst_credits_exhausted
[09:12:13] admission_controller: request_id=abc161 account=cartomart pool=carto-prod-us tokens=300 status=deny reason=headroom_insufficient
```

And billing/accounting trace:

```
[09:12:14] accounting: account=cartomart pool=carto-prod-us tokens_charged=123456 last_credit_balance=0 credit_refill_attempt=failed err=authz-billing-lag
[09:12:15] accounting: account=cartomart delta_credits=-25000 note=unexpected_debit
```

They also saw 502s from our proxy for some streaming connections.

deploy-bot: A rollout of svc/accounting v1.3.4 completed 2025-11-10T08:58:49Z to carto-prod-us (metadata: roll-id=rl-3221).

li (eng-infra): Noted. Two things to check: 1) autoscaler timeline (did it see the surge and make a decision), 2) admission controller policy thresholds (burst window and headroom fraction). I'm querying the autoscaler events now.

sam (eng-runtime): I saw earlier evidence of a noisy long-running streaming job occupying a large fraction of GPU slots in carto-prod-us around the same window. If streaming sessions hold the KV cache or pins GPU for entire response, that can starve short completions. Can someone grab `nvidia-smi` and the runtime process list for 09:10-09:20? Also check model variants in use — fallback to a smaller variant would reduce token consumption.

ana (sre): Running a quick aggregation of admission_denied reasons across the pool for that minute: majority reason=burst_credits_exhausted (62%), headroom_insufficient (28%), auth_rate_limit (10%). Suggest immediate mitigations: temporary refill of cartomart burst credits, relax headroom threshold from 20%->10% for 5 minutes, enable fallback (redwood-small) as automatic model fallback for their routes.

zach (billing): Looking at accounting: v1.3.4 changed token rounding for streaming chunks which inflated token accounting by ~2.1x in some cases (we're seeing this in debug flags). That would explain unexpected debit. We should: 1) temporarily credit cartomart for the overcharge, 2) roll back the token calculation or ship hotfix, 3) reconcile historical deltas. I'll prepare a credit delta and a billing note.

li (eng-infra): Autoscaler events: it saw increased queue length at 09:12:05 but decision latency was ~45s due to cooldown + max-scale-step=1. We only had 2 spare nodes in the region; scale-out required allocation of a new GPU node which hit EC2 quota delay (provisioning 90s). Suggest increasing max-scale-step during predictable marketing blasts or enabling a pre-warmed burst buffer.

sam (eng-runtime): Evidence for noisy neighbor: runtime traces show 7 long-running streaming handles from account=streaming_partner that were active 09:08->09:20 and pinned GPU memory ~70% each; those jobs serialized small token writes but held the session open. They collided with CartoMart's short requests. Recommend: enforce session timeout for streaming of 60s, and prefer CPU-based streaming workers for long tail jobs.

maya (support): CartoMart asks for root cause and quick mitigation. They want their credits restored and a plan so this doesn't repeat before their next campaign.

ana (sre): Proposed immediate playbook (temporary):
- [ ] credit cartomart +25k tokens (zach)
- [ ] set headroom threshold ->10% for carto-prod-us for 10m (li)
- [ ] enable model fallback mapping carto-prod-us -> redwood-small for the account (sam)
- [ ] revoke long-running streaming sessions for streaming_partner and notify them (sre + infra)
- [ ] open postmortem and schedule change to autoscaler step and prewarm buffer (owners: ana + li + runtime)

jon (oncall): I'll own the incident channel and coordinate with CartoMart. I'll send the temporary changes now and monitor metrics (admission accepts, 429 rate, latency p95) for 30m.

zach (billing): Done: provisional credit +25000 tokens applied (note=proactive-incident-credit). I'll follow up with reconciliation after hotfix.

li (eng-infra): Headroom tweak applied to carto-prod-us (ephemeral) and autoscaler max-step adjusted for the region. Monitor.

sam (eng-runtime): Fallback rule active. Also killed 8 stale streaming handles that were pinning GPUs. Observed immediate drop in GPU utilization from 92% -> 48%.

maya (support): CartoMart reports reduced 429s and latency back to normal; they're grateful. They asked for a short RCA and a permanent plan to avoid this.

ana (sre): Next steps / action items for RCA:
- run unbiased accounting recon for 09:00-09:30 to quantify overcharge (zach)
- patch token calculation in v1.3.4 (billing + release)
- change autoscaler policy: increase max-scale-step for critical pools, add prewarm buffer config (li)
- enforce streaming session timeout and rate limits for long-lived sessions (sam)
- add admission controller metric alerts for rapid burst credit drain (ana)

jon (oncall): Closing loop: CartoMart is stable. Will open a postmortem ticket and ping relevant teams. Thanks all :heart:

maya (support): Thanks team — logging this thread into the support ticket and sending the customers the credit confirmation and incident summary.
